title: Sharp Dimension Dependence for the Last Iterate of the SubGradient Method
summary: We study the last iterate of the projected subGradient Method (sGM) for convex Lipschitz objectives defined on $\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that, for a finite horizon $n$ and a constant stepsize $η=Θ(1/\sqrt n)$, the last iterate achieves an optimization error of order $d/\sqrt n$, showing that the extra $\log n$ factor appearing in high dimensions is unnecessary in every fixed dimension. We complement this result with a matching linear-in-$d$ lower bound and show that the sharp worst-case dimension-horizon dependence is of order $\min\{d,\log n\}/\sqrt n$.
